Subject: Post-demo recap — deployment-mode tradeoffs & dedicated sizing clarifications

Thanks for the demo time today, Samir — good discussion. Quick recap from our side and a short set of clarifying questions so we can size the dedicated path versus Hosted / Private VPC options: 

Summary (from today's demo)
- Primary workload: patient-facing summarization + anonymized retrieval (low input PII, PHI-stored downstream)
- Latency target: interactive (sub-second p95 where possible) for the most-frequent endpoints
- Compliance: production data needs to be in a customer-managed VPC; non-prod can be Hosted

Clarifying questions (short answers appreciated):
1) Peak TPS (sustained) and short burst TPS we should plan for? (e.g., 75 TPS sustained, 200 TPS burst)
2) Avg/median request token mix: avg prompt tokens, avg completion tokens, and percent that are long (>1024 tokens)
3) Concurrency semantics: do you need 1:1 sessions pinned, or best-effort concurrency (we optimize with batching/KV)?
4) P95 latency SLO for the endpoints that will be on Dedicated vs acceptable tail for Hosted fallback
5) Any hard requirements for KMS/BYOK, audit log retention, or region constraints beyond "US"?

Attached a short sizing worksheet (redwood-dedicated-sizing-template.xlsx) — if you can drop in the traffic trace (olive-traffic-sample.json) or numbers above, we can run a quick capacity estimate and propose GPU SKU mixes (cost-first and latency-first options).

Suggested next steps:
- You fill the worksheet or reply with the answers above
- We'll run a short projection and propose 2 SKU mixes (latency-optimized, cost-optimized) + an ops checklist for VPC onboarding
- If suitable, schedule a 1-hour sizing workshop next week with Ops/Infra folks

Thanks — looping in Marissa for workshop coordination and Monica for security/compliance follow-ups.

— Marcus

Thanks Marcus — appreciate the clear recap. Below are the answers (we scoped this with the infra team this morning):

1) Traffic profile
- Typical daytime sustained TPS: 18 TPS across all endpoints
- Peak sustained TPS (end-of-month reports / campaigns): ~75 TPS sustained for 2–6 hour windows
- Short bursts (marketing / batch jobs): up to 220 TPS for a few minutes occasionally

2) Token mix (approx)
- Avg prompt tokens: 120
- Avg completion tokens: 250
- ~8% of requests exceed 1,024 tokens (mainly long summary jobs)

3) Concurrency
- We expect ~20 simultaneous interactive sessions for clinical staff during peak; background jobs can be batched. We are fine with best-effort concurrency as long as p95 latency stays within SLOs for interactive endpoints.

4) Latency SLOs
- Interactive endpoints: p95 <= 300ms preferred (hard requirement: <=500ms)
- Background summarization: p95 <= 2s is acceptable

5) Compliance / security
- Production must run in our VPC (customer-managed) with KMS BYOK for encryption at rest; non-prod can be hosted.
- SOC2 required; attaching a pointer to our security intake (SOC2-evidence-stub.pdf) and the platform team's contact (platform@olivehealth.com).

Timeline: aim to move to an initial Dedicated pilot in 6–8 weeks if the sizing checks out.

I uploaded a week of representative traces to the drive link you gave (folder: 1a2b3c-olive-traces). Let me know if you need raw logs or anonymized request bodies.

— Samir

Great dataset — thanks Samir, this is exactly what we need. Quick read and our initial take + proposed plan: 

Initial sizing thoughts (high level)
- Given the 75 TPS peak + 220 TPS short bursts and your p95 <= 300ms target for interactive endpoints, we recommend starting with a Dedicated pool that emphasizes latency with an ops-safe fallback to Hosted variants for non-critical traffic.
- Two SKU mixes we'll model: 
  A) Latency-optimized: 4 x A100-80GB inference nodes (low-latency kernels, larger KV cache). This favors lower p95 at higher cost.
  B) Cost-optimized: 12 x A10G-style inference nodes with aggressive batching and prefix caching to hit sustained 75 TPS at lower cost, with occasional burst scaling to handle short spikes.

Notes on architecture and tradeoffs
- KV/prefix caching will reduce token compute on repeated contexts (clinical templates) — this benefits A10G options more for cost savings.
- Heavy long-tail requests (>1k tokens) will push memory needs; the A100-80GB config gives headroom for those workloads without model splits.
- For your BYOK/KMS requirement and VPC onboarding: our Private deployment (VPC/private control plane) supports customer-managed keys and audit log forwarding; Monica will follow up with the security checklist for the procurement team.

Immediate next steps (proposed)
1) Marcus + I run the sizing worksheet you filled and convert traces to token-level projections (we'll do that today).
2) Schedule a 60-minute sizing workshop next Tue or Wed with your infra + security (we're flexible) — proposed slots: Tue May 4 10:00–11:00 PT or Wed May 5 13:00–14:00 PT.
3) If the team is comfortable with the projection, we'll spin a short Dedicated pilot (2 weeks) with monitoring hooks and rollback to Hosted for non-prod traffic.

Action items: Samir — confirm which workshop slot works and attach the worksheet populated if convenient. Monica — I flagged security checklist and BYOK runbook (see related Drive link).

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through the two SKU mixes once Marcus has the projection ready.
